critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1885 lines — even more overdue for router split (auth, profile, lessons, billing, checkin, challenge, onboarding, daily-path, retention, referral, mission). Mission added ~120 more lines.

POST /api/mission/progress accepts arbitrary `increment` value with no upper bound — a malicious client could send {task:'chat', increment:999} and instantly cross the target on the first call, still getting only the spec'd 5 XP (so no XP exploit), but task_progress.chat would jump to 999 in mongo. Consider clamping increment to <=task.target or to a sane max like 5.

/api/mission/progress writes both (a) task_progress.chat += inc and (b) task_done.chat=true + xp_earned += xp in TWO separate update_one calls (lines 1642 and 1652). If the second update fails after the first succeeds, the doc would show progress>=target but task_done=false and xp not credited, creating a stuck state on retry (the next call would re-increment and re-cross, but xp_awarded would still come back 5 — it self-heals, OK). Could be tightened with a single $set+$inc with conditional write.

MissionCard.jsx auto-fetches /mission/today on every dashboard mount with no caching. Combined with the existing Dashboard fetch + StreakMilestoneModal fetch + UpgradeNudgeModal fetch + auth/me fetch, dashboard cold-load makes 5+ requests. React Query / SWR dedup would help.

Mission.jsx 4 sub-step components (Chat/Vocab/Speak/Write) likely live in one file — if so, please split when over 700 lines. Auto-advance after XP flash is hardcoded to ~1.1s — make it a const for tweakability.

Completion screen shows '+1 day' streak hardcoded in UI even though the actual streak delta depends on update_streak_and_xp's same-day vs new-day logic. If the user already had a streak today (e.g., from a checkin earlier), the completion UI's '+1 day' would be misleading.
Practice page is a flat gallery — for premium upsell consistency, consider greying out / locking modes that have free-tier limits hit (e.g., conversation when daily 5 used).
